title: Characteristics of turbulent flow and methods of analysis: telling turbulence from other irregular motion, and what can be done once a flow qualifies
status: reviewed and locally validated; passes 1-9 complete; gate 6b round 2 had 1 blocking defect, fixed by a reviser and checked by the lead (no round 3)
transcript_provenance: Local machine transcription (faster-whisper small.en); not publisher captions
source_uncertainties: ASR spellings in the transcripts: 'Tannicus and Lamley' is Tennekes and Lumley; 'Biswersk' (L7 about 820 s) is Boussinesq; 'Es-Sahli' and the other source names were read from the Sources slide (an extra frame extracted at 141 s of L6, helper file outside the repository), not from the transcript.

The Navier-Stokes equation written on L6 f0045 and f0047 (U_t + U.grad U = -(1/rho) grad P + nu lap U) uses a handwritten vector glyph that could be read as U or V; the speech says u; the chapter writes U, as in chapters 1 and 6.
L6 f0051 and f0055 write Dw/Dt = (w.grad)U + nu lap w with the stretching term circled; the board form w.grad U and the speech agree.
L7 f0013 writes Kn = lambda/l (handwritten) and the speech says 'lambda over L'; the chapter follows chapter 6 (Kn = lambda_m / l_g).
L7 f0030 writes tau = mu du/dy and tau_t = mu_t d(u)/dy with an overbar on the mean strain; the chapter writes nu_T and (3.10).

L7 f0042 and f0049: the legend of the compiled spectra is small and was read together with Figure 3 of Saddoughi (1993, p. 245); the slide reads 'Laufer 1954, pipe 170' where the report reads 'Laufer 1952'. The slide's ordinate is E11/(eps nu^5)^(1/4) (read on f0042); the report prints E11(k1 eta)/(eps nu)^(1/2). The positions at which the curves leave the common curve are readings from the figure, uncertain by a factor of 2 to 3.

The L7 dissipation slide (f0002) names gravity waves in planetary atmospheres and acoustic noise; the ocean-wave example is on the L6 vorticity slide (f0057). The chapter's wave calculation is for a deep-water surface wave and does not treat either of the dissipation slide's examples.

The journal article of Saddoughi and Veeravalli (1994), Pope (2000), Tennekes and Lumley (1972), Bakker (2008), Chapman (1979) and Burgers's paper were not obtained; statements attributed to them are as the lecture or the sources opened give them.

Assumed inputs, not from the lecture or a source: bearing film (50 micrometres, 5 m/s, nu = 1e-4 m2/s), river (1 m, 1 m/s, nu = 1e-6 m2/s), chimney wind 5 m/s, ten times larger Gamma at cruise altitude as an upper bound, water viscosity 1e-6 m2/s for the swell and the liquid jet.

sections.section: The objects of the chapter and the running case
sections.lecture_material: Navier-Stokes equations as written on the slide; the round jet of chapters 6-8 and 10.
sections.research_extension: U.S. Standard Atmosphere (1976), Table 10: air properties.
sections.teaching_construction: Definitions of attribute, test and excluded motion; notation Kn, nu_T.

sections.section: Laminar flow is the exception, and large Reynolds numbers are the rule in the lecture's examples
sections.lecture_material: List of natural and engineering flows; laminar flow is the exception; lubricating oil in a bearing.
sections.teaching_construction: Reynolds numbers of the jet and of an assumed bearing film and river.

sections.section: Irregularity is shared by the motions the lecture excludes
sections.lecture_material: Irregular, seemingly random, chaotic; Tennekes and Lumley as quoted; deterministic equations versus random flow.
sections.teaching_construction: Separation of statistical description from stochastic equations; irregularity as necessary and not sufficient.

sections.section: Diffusivity: how fast a patch of fluid spreads
sections.lecture_material: Diffusivity test, spillway and contrail and chimney examples, list of applications.
sections.research_extension: Kaercher (2018): Table 1, ice supersaturation, wind shear, turbulent mixing in the plume and wake.
sections.teaching_construction: Effective diffusivity K and its ratio to Gamma; jet Peclet number; laminar plume width; contrail widths against molecular spread.

sections.section: Large Reynolds numbers: a wide range of sizes between inertia and viscosity
sections.lecture_material: Instability at large Re; interaction of viscous and inertial terms; nonlinearity makes the equations nearly intractable.
sections.teaching_construction: Three Reynolds numbers of the jet; l_0/eta = Re_0^(3/4) = 1.27e3; grading of the intractability statement.

sections.section: Three-dimensional vorticity fluctuations: what stretching does to size
sections.lecture_material: Turbulence is rotational; vorticity transport equation; stretching absent in 2D; cyclones and ocean waves are not turbulent.
sections.research_extension: None (back-reference to chapter 6 and Boffetta and Ecke via chapter 6).
sections.teaching_construction: Stretched-vortex solution with core radius (4 nu/a)^(1/2) = 2 eta at the Kolmogorov strain rate; grading of 'breakup'.

sections.section: Dissipation: the one process that removes energy
sections.lecture_material: Dissipative; kinetic energy to heat; dies out without supply; waves and sound are not dissipative.
sections.research_extension: McComb and co-authors (2015): C_epsilon asymptote 0.468 (manuscript p. 1).
sections.teaching_construction: Energy budget of a periodic box; dissipation of a linear deep-water wave, decay rate 4 nu kappa^2; loss times in own time scales; heating rate.

sections.section: The continuum attribute and the smallest eddies
sections.lecture_material: Continuum phenomenon; Knudsen number lambda/L much less than 1.
sections.research_extension: U.S. Standard Atmosphere (1976), Table 10: mean free path, mean molecular speed, viscosity.
sections.teaching_construction: Kn_eta = 1.545 Ma Re_0^(-1/4) for air; jet value 8.4e-4; failure example.

sections.section: Turbulence is a property of flows, not of fluids
sections.lecture_material: Turbulence is not a feature of fluids but of flows; same dynamics in all fluids at large Re; each flow unique.
sections.research_extension: None (back-reference to chapter 6 on Reynolds-number similarity).
sections.teaching_construction: Fluid enters only through Re within the model; equal-Re jet in a liquid; limits (Mach, scalar, buoyancy).

sections.section: No general approach: the families of flows and the closure problem
sections.lecture_material: No general approach; equations need empirical data; more unknowns than equations; ad hoc assumptions.
sections.teaching_construction: Grading of the four statements against the count of chapter 9 and the channel test.

sections.section: A model need not be complete: the eddy viscosity as the lecture's case in point
sections.lecture_material: Spirited inventors (as quoted); eddy viscosity and mixing length by analogy with molecular transport; flow versus fluid property; LES.
sections.teaching_construction: Scale-separation comparison (Kn of the molecular law against eddy size over gradient length); eddy viscosity as a flow property.

sections.section: Dimensional analysis: the form follows, the constant does not
sections.lecture_material: Dimensional analysis and Buckingham's Pi theorem; inertial subrange of the spectrum as the example.
sections.teaching_construction: Null-space statement of the Pi groups; far field of a round jet from the momentum flux; groups of the plotted spectrum; exponent -5/3.

sections.section: Asymptotic invariance: what a limit can and cannot remove
sections.lecture_material: High-Re descriptions must behave properly as Re tends to infinity; Reynolds-number similarity of the boundary layer; jet at 1e6 or 2e6.
sections.research_extension: Lee and Moser (2015) channel DNS at Re_tau 543.5, 1000.5, 5185.9.
sections.teaching_construction: Spread of mean-velocity quantities over the three simulations (Table 3.1); region-specific invariance.

sections.section: Local invariance and the compiled spectra
sections.lecture_material: Local invariance; Kolmogorov-scaled spectra of many flows overlap except at small wavenumber; inertial subrange in the overlap.
sections.teaching_construction: Slide axes as the Pi groups; grading of 'overlaps entirely'; insensitivity of the log-log plot to a 20 % error in epsilon.
Energy budget, wave decay, loss times, Kn_eta, stretched vortex, Pi groups, channel spreads.
